summary: The @gyomu/schema package provides a unified framework for domain-driven data modeling and robust error handling built on top of Effect. It enables the automatic generation of CRUD schema suites from entity definitions, manages complex domain validation, and provides structural analysis for TypeScript source code. This comprehensive toolkit ensures data integrity, consistent error diagnostics, and standardized API results across the system.
responsibilities: Define and maintain formal entity schemas for business domain objects.
Automate the generation of validation-ready CRUD schemas from domain definitions.
Provide a consistent cross-layer error handling and diagnostic context strategy.
Model TypeScript source code structures to support documentation and static analysis.
Standardize data transformation and result handling via schema-based decoding.
Implement core infrastructure for operational policies, logging, and retry logic.

capabilities.name: Entity Modeling
capabilities.description: Definition of domain entities and their fields, providing the foundation for automated schema generation and UI annotations.

capabilities.name: CRUD Schema Generation
capabilities.description: Automatic creation of validated schemas for insert, update, and select operations based on central entity definitions.

capabilities.name: Structured Error Handling
capabilities.description: Consistent error classification and diagnostic metadata injection across system layers with support for retryability and observability.

capabilities.name: TypeScript Analysis Framework
capabilities.description: Structural modeling of TypeScript source code metadata, including symbols, dependencies, and type compositions for automated tooling.

capabilities.name: Validation and Conversion
capabilities.description: Tools for decoding, transforming, and validating data inputs using Effect-based schemas and custom type guards.

capabilities.name: Operational Infrastructure
capabilities.description: Foundational utilities for result handling, JSON schema structures, logging, and runtime execution environments.

designDecisions: Utilization of the Effect library for robust functional composition and error management.
Decoupling of business logic from data representation through auto-generated schema suites.
Use of branded types to enforce domain-specific safety at the type system level.
Centralization of error traits to ensure uniform observability and handling policies throughout the application.
Recursive modeling of JSON and TypeScript structures to handle complex, nested metadata.
usageGuidance: Define domain entities using the provided schema builder patterns to benefit from automated CRUD and validation logic.
Use standard GyomuError types and contexts when defining new domain failures to maintain consistency.
Leverage the TypeScript analysis schemas for building code-related tools or documentation generators.
Always wrap external integrations in the standardized ResultSchema pattern to ensure predictable API responses.
Utilize provided field utilities for common data types like dates and branded identifiers to ensure consistent transformation logic.
